# Faithful Markdown Export for Confluence

> A Confluence Cloud app that exports a page, a page tree or an entire space to
> Markdown in one pass — attachments carried along with body references rewritten,
> page titles kept as readable filenames, and a report naming everything that had to
> be degraded. Confluence's own export, in beta since June 2026, returns the body
> text of one page and writes no files; this app is for the case where a whole space
> has to arrive somewhere else intact. Its one rule is "degrade, never delete": what
> Markdown cannot express is flattened, never dropped. Every release is scored
> against a public, reproducible conformance suite of 63 rules.

Built by Second Tiger. Runs entirely on Atlassian infrastructure: the app contacts
no external service, stores nothing, and requests read access only.

## What it is for

Teams migrating a Confluence space into a Git repository, a static site, or an
LLM pipeline — that is, people who need the tree and the attachments, not one
page. A single page is already served by Confluence's own Export menu.

Two things make a bulk export go wrong, and both are silent. The first is scope:
an export that returns body text leaves the images, the inter-page links and the
folder structure to be rebuilt by hand. The second is damage — a completed task
comes out unchecked, a Korean or Japanese page title becomes a UUID filename, a
code block forgets it was Python, a code block inside a list item escapes the
list. None of these raise an error.

## How it differs from Confluence's own Markdown export

| | Confluence native export (beta) | Faithful Markdown Export |
|---|---|---|
| One page's body as Markdown | yes | yes |
| Page tree or whole space in one pass | no, one page at a time | yes |
| Attachments, with body references rewritten | no | yes |
| Links between exported pages | left pointing at the wiki | rewritten relative |
| Filenames from page titles | not applicable, no files written | the title, non-Latin included |
| Report of what was degraded | no | yes, naming the page |

## Measured results

The 63 rules divide into 46 that ask whether the text survived the conversion and
17 that ask whether the files on disk are right — attachments, filenames, folder
tree. Confluence's native export writes no files, so those 17 cannot be scored
against it and are left out rather than counted as failures.

| Export | Measured | Conversion (46) | Critical failures | Files (17) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Faithful Markdown Export 0.1.0 | 2026-09-16 | 46/46 | 0 | 17/17 |
| Confluence native export (beta) | 2026-10-14 | 35/46 | 3 | not applicable |
| Markdown Exporter for Confluence 3.5.0 | 2026-09-16 | 34/46 | 5 | 12/17 |

Over all 63 rules, where that is meaningful: Faithful 63/63 with 0 critical
failures, Markdown Exporter 3.5.0 46/63 with 9.

The native export was measured through the same API its Export menu calls
(`GET /wiki/api/v2/pages/{id}?body-format=markdown`), one page at a time across the
whole seeded corpus space. Its three critical conversion failures are a fence inside a
code block closing the block early, a code block escaping its list item, and an
expand block losing its title.

The corpus, the 63 rules, the scorer and both app exports of the same space are
public, so the comparison can be reproduced rather than taken on trust.

## Measured performance

- 1,000 pages: 3 minutes 40 seconds
- 138 MB of attachments: 5 minutes 40 seconds

The bottleneck is bytes, not page count.

## Pricing

- Up to 10 users: free
- 11 users and above: per-user, with a 30-day free trial on paid tiers

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://youngjunekwon.github.io/faithful-markdown-export/docs.html): how to run an export, what the zip contains, how each Confluence construct is converted, and what the app cannot do
- [Privacy](https://youngjunekwon.github.io/faithful-markdown-export/privacy.html): what the app reads and what it stores, which is nothing
- [Security](https://youngjunekwon.github.io/faithful-markdown-export/security.html): scopes, data handling, and what happens when something goes wrong
- [Support](https://youngjunekwon.github.io/faithful-markdown-export/support.html): how to reach a human

## Verification

- [Conformance suite](https://github.com/YoungjuneKwon/confluence-markdown-conformance): seed a Confluence space with a fixed corpus, export it with any app, and score the output against 63 rules
- [Both exports of the same space](https://github.com/YoungjuneKwon/confluence-markdown-conformance/tree/main/samples): read the difference instead of the scores

- [Atlassian Marketplace listing](https://marketplace.atlassian.com/apps/1569868747/faithful-markdown-export-for-confluence): install, pricing tiers, and trial
